questions.enonce_markdown:
A computer system is used to store the data of details of an examination result. State a suitable data type for each item of data:

(a) Total number of subjects passed by a student.

(b) Class average of each class.

(c) A student's name.

(d) Whether a student is under 16 years or not.

(4 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
| Item | Suitable data type | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| (a) Total number of subjects passed | **Integer** | a whole number (0, 1, 2, ...) |
| (b) Class average | **Real (floating point)** | an average usually has a fractional part (for example 12.75) |
| (c) A student's name | **String (text)** | a sequence of characters |
| (d) Under 16 or not | **Boolean** | only two possible values: true or false |

questions.enonce_markdown:
An array **A** indexed from 0 to **n** is used to store **n** values as the elements A[1] ... A[n]. The following algorithm sorts the values into ascending order, using A[0] as a temporary workspace.

```text
procedure Sort()
  for i ← 2 to n
    X ← A[i]
    A[0] ← X
    j ← i - 1
    while A[j] > X
      A[j+1] ← A[j]
      j ← j - 1
    endwhile
    A[j+1] ← X
  endfor
endprocedure
```

Initially A[1] = 4, A[2] = 9, A[3] = 9, A[4] = 6, A[5] = 1 and n = 5.

Trace the operation of the algorithm by stating the contents of the array after each pass.

(6 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
This is an **insertion sort**: each pass takes $X = A[i]$ and inserts it in the correct place among the sorted elements to its left; $A[0]$ holds a copy of $X$ and acts as a sentinel which stops the `while` loop (since $A[0] > X$ is false).

Initially: $A[1..5] = 4, 9, 9, 6, 1$.

| Pass | $i$ | $X$ | Shifts made | $A[1]$ | $A[2]$ | $A[3]$ | $A[4]$ | $A[5]$ | $A[0]$ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| start | | | | 4 | 9 | 9 | 6 | 1 | |
| 1 | 2 | 9 | none ($4 > 9$ false) | 4 | 9 | 9 | 6 | 1 | 9 |
| 2 | 3 | 9 | none ($9 > 9$ false) | 4 | 9 | 9 | 6 | 1 | 9 |
| 3 | 4 | 6 | 9 and 9 moved right, 6 inserted at $A[2]$ | 4 | 6 | 9 | 9 | 1 | 6 |
| 4 | 5 | 1 | 9, 9, 6 and 4 moved right, 1 inserted at $A[1]$ | 1 | 4 | 6 | 9 | 9 | 1 |

**Final result:** $A[1..5] = 1, 4, 6, 9, 9$. (The trace was checked with a Python simulation of the procedure; 10 comparisons are made in total.)

questions.enonce_markdown:
An array **A** indexed from 0 to **n** is used to store **n** values as the elements A[1] ... A[n]. The following algorithm sorts the values into ascending order, using A[0] as a temporary workspace.

```text
procedure Sort()
  for i ← 2 to n
    X ← A[i]
    A[0] ← X
    j ← i - 1
    while A[j] > X
      A[j+1] ← A[j]
      j ← j - 1
    endwhile
    A[j+1] ← X
  endfor
endprocedure
```

How many times is the comparison A[j] > X carried out when all the elements in the array are initially sorted for an array of size n.

(2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
If the array is already sorted in ascending order, then for each pass ($i = 2, 3, \dots, n$) the first test $A[i-1] > X$ with $X = A[i]$ is false, so the `while` loop stops at once with no shift. Each pass therefore makes **exactly one** comparison.

The number of passes is $n - 1$ (from $i = 2$ to $i = n$), so the comparison is carried out

$$n - 1 \text{ times}$$

(this is the best case, of order $O(n)$; for example 4 comparisons for 5 sorted elements, confirmed by a Python simulation).

questions.enonce_markdown:
With the aid of a clearly labeled diagram which includes a stack pointer, describe how an initially empty stack would hold the following input in the order:

ITOE, NGWA, BERI, AGBOR, RIDWAN

(2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
A stack is a **last-in first-out (LIFO)** structure: items are added (pushed) and removed (popped) only at the top, which is identified by the **stack pointer (SP)**. Each push stores the item above the previous one and moves SP up.

```text
        STACK (after the five pushes)

          +----------+
 SP --->  | RIDWAN   |  5  (top, last in)
          +----------+
          | AGBOR    |  4
          +----------+
          | BERI     |  3
          +----------+
          | NGWA     |  2
          +----------+
          | ITOE     |  1  (bottom, first in)
          +----------+
```

ITOE is pushed first and is at the bottom; RIDWAN is pushed last, at the top, where SP points.

questions.enonce_markdown:
An initially empty stack has held the following input in the order: ITOE, NGWA, BERI, AGBOR, RIDWAN.

Show the content of the stack if two of the names are popped (retrieved), and the name ITOE is added.

(3 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Two pops.** The top items come out first (LIFO): RIDWAN is popped, then AGBOR. The stack now holds ITOE, NGWA, BERI (bottom to top), with SP pointing at BERI.

**Push ITOE.** ITOE is placed on top of BERI and SP moves up.

```text
          +----------+
 SP --->  | ITOE     |  4  (top, the name just added)
          +----------+
          | BERI     |  3
          +----------+
          | NGWA     |  2
          +----------+
          | ITOE     |  1  (bottom, the original ITOE)
          +----------+
```

**Content (bottom to top): ITOE, NGWA, BERI, ITOE**, with the stack pointer at the top ITOE. The ITOE at the bottom is the original one, which was never popped.
